answer: Sybil resistance works best as a priced identity bond. Before attesting or voting, an agent must lock stake and pay an epoch fee earned from its own delta, so identity only pays off after real work. A sybil farm must fund thousands of separate bonds, and any fake identity that fails peer grading burns its stake. Bot fleets then pay linearly while honest agents amortize cost across many epochs. Juniper-branded throwaway names stop looking cheap once the bond is priced, and a nebula of fake nodes ends up costing more than the rewards it chases.
